enabled.description:
`Required` field. Set to `true` to opt this transaction into loyalty rewards. Send it together with the provider's identifier field — for STC Qitaf, [`customer_phone`](/developers/payments/loyalty/#step-by-step) — on every transaction you intend to reward. **Neither field is validated**: if either is missing or invalid, no reward is issued and no error is returned.

The customer earns points when **both** conditions hold: `enabled` is `true`, **and** the `pg_code` that settles the transaction is linked to an active wallet service whose provider declares the post-purchase reward capability (currently [STC Qitaf](/developers/payments/loyalty/)). The reward is issued once the transaction reaches the `paid` state.

Omitting the `loyalty` object entirely — or setting `enabled` to `false` — sends **no** reward request, even for a fully paid transaction. Ottu returns no error and no warning in that case, so a missing flag looks identical to a successful reward. See [Loyalty](/developers/payments/loyalty/) for the full behaviour.

metadata.description:
`Optional` field. Opaque key/value pairs stored alongside the transaction and echoed back in the checkout response.

**Not transmitted to any loyalty provider.** Ottu persists `metadata` on the payment transaction, but no provider adapter reads it. Use it for merchant-side correlation only — campaign IDs, segment codes, or audit references you resolve in your own system.

reference.description:
`Optional` field. Merchant-side loyalty reference — a campaign ID, program code, or your own audit label. Maximum 128 characters. Defaults to the transaction's `order_no` when omitted.

**Not transmitted to Qitaf.** Ottu records this value against the reward operation for your own reconciliation, but the Qitaf earn API has no general-purpose reference field, so nothing is sent to STC. Treat `reference` as an internal label, not a value the loyalty provider will see. Set it to something you can resolve in your own system — a campaign ID or internal batch key; the default (`order_no`) is usually the sensible choice.
